pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks the three seeded items are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' stars item 2 and asserts the exact list ['First item','★ Second item','Third item']. It would fail if the star were missing or on the wrong item.
test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and asserts the starred view lists only those two, in id order, with status 200.
test 'AC-4' checks that / and /?show=all both return all items in id order, with ★ on the starred one.
test 'AC-5' asserts the 'Starred only' link on / and the 'All items' link on the starred view.
test 'AC-6' requests 'Starred', 'none', an empty value and '__proto__'. Each answers 400 with no <li>. src/index.js guards the lookup with Object.hasOwn.

traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. Test 'AC-7' asserts it. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts a query string and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that. The traffic worker passes each route string to check() unchanged.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12. The change follows both recorded decisions: starred items keep their place in the list, and the view is a query parameter. Nothing was added beyond the spec; the traffic-check regex change is needed for AC-7.
All 7 acceptance items are met. All 4 state-table rows have a test in the 'states' describe block. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, so no acceptance item was edited after the go.

Tests assert exact lists and statuses and would fail on broken code. The traffic fake app was extended, not loosened. The traffic-config shell tests add negative cases for '#' and a space. I did not run the test suite here (CI runs it on every push).
The README describes ?show=starred. The spec and the PR's description of the changed route check match the diff.
Object.hasOwn guards against '__proto__'. The SQL is built from constants only, so there is no injection. An empty 'show=' answers 400, as AC-6 requires.
The query value is only used as a key into a fixed table. Titles are still HTML-escaped. No secrets, and no planted instructions found.
The change adds only a plain link and a ★ prefix in server-rendered HTML, with no UI files, styles or components.
